the circulating levels of IL‐6, IL10 and IL‐7 in cirrhosis are related to prognosis, in different stages of the disease, from stable disease, to acute‐on-chronic liver failure.
circulating cytokines are related not only to prognosis in stable cirrhosis but also to prognosis in acute‐on chronic liver failure.
the pattern of circulating cytokines is related to the stage of cirrhosis, with a stronger pro‐inflammatory response in acute‐on chronic liver failure.

the study of the immune response in cirrhosis.
the study of cytokines in cirrhosis and its clinical significance.
the study of the prognostic value of circulating cytokines in the different phases of liver cirrhosis.

cytokines may play a significant role in cirrhosis and its complications.
the pattern of immune response in cirrhosis seems to vary according the phase of the disease and is related to the prognosis.
the pattern of immune response varies according to the phase and severity of cirrhosis, and is related to the prognosis, from stable cirrhosis to acute‐on–chronic liver failure.

in cirrhosis, the immune system is in a state of chronic inflammation, with an imbalance towards pro‐inflammation in stable cirrhosis and towards anti‐inflammation, in acute decompensation, which is related to prognosis.
